items.detail: Oracle Free (Oracle AI Database 26ai Free Release 23.26.4.0.0 - Develop, Learn, and Run for Free Version 23.26.4.0.0), NLS_CHARACTERSET=AL32UTF8, schema ispf_aa
replica A and replica B actuator health UP
admin login on A and on B
a token issued by A is accepted by B and the reverse (sessions in the shared Oracle database)

both JVMs (docker inspect): single-engine on, history + journal JDBC, cluster on, NATS + JetStream on, Redis on, warm off, ddl-auto=none; one ISPF_DB schema (ispf_aa); replica ids oracle-aa-a / oracle-aa-b; capabilities http-public,ws,replica-sync,config-write,schedulers,drivers
flyway Oracle/V1 applied once (success=1), no failed rows
Hibernate OracleDialect with ddl-auto=none on both JVMs
cluster + single-engine passes the Oracle boot fences (pre-Flyway and on context refresh) on both JVMs
ispf session: AL32UTF8; single-engine preflight passed on both JVMs
ClusterDependencyValidator on both JVMs: Cluster dependency check OK (jetStream=true, redis=true, liveMirror=true, pathInterest=true)
both JVM containers on UTC; Oracle system_time_zone UTC, time_zone SYSTEM (leases are zone-less DATETIME(6))
GET /platform/cluster/health on A and on B: clusterEnabled, nodesUp=2/2, liveVariableSync on, NATS on
platform_cluster_replicas: oracle-aa-a,oracle-aa-b with a heartbeat in the last 60 s
device created on A visible on B after 31 ms; deleted on A, gone on B after 20 ms (no ghost)

variables lagProbe and aa (historized) and event aagate defined on A; after the object-level PATCH on A, B reloaded the object from Oracle and serves both definitions (writable, aa historyEnabled) in 28 ms
WebSocket observer subscribed on each replica (/ws/objects, cluster path interest in Redis): PUT on A read on B in 1320 ms, PUT on B read on A in 1434 ms (8 consecutive reads each, SLO 5000 ms)
PUT 101.5 on A and 202.5 on B: exactly 1 variable_samples row each (no mirrored duplicate); GET /history on A and on B returns both
POST /events/fire on A and on B: exactly 2 event_history rows (1 per fire, no mirrored duplicate); GET /events?before= on A and on B lists both
20 concurrent POST /objects (10 on A, 10 on B): all 2xx, 20 object_nodes rows, each replica sees the other's objects
20 concurrent DELETE /objects across both JVMs (each deletes the other's objects): audit_event_chain 3 -> 23; GET /audit/verify-chain intact on A and on B
virtual driver configured and started through A (RUNNING): one platform_driver_locks row, holder oracle-aa-a, live
B sees driverId=virtual before kill (wait 7 ms)
docker kill A (no graceful release): B reclaimed the driver lease in 8.1 s (TTL 15 s, scan 5 s, SLO 45 s); driver RUNNING on B
with A down: B answers /info and login, and its historian and journal writes land in Oracle (1 sample row, 1 event row)

before the kill 6 live short-TTL leases on 1 holder(s) [alert_rule_periodic,application_sql_bindings,platform_scheduler,process_program_runner,workflow_due_timer_scheduler,workflow_retry_scheduler]; 45 s after it 6 live, all on one holder (the survivor) [alert_rule_periodic,application_sql_bindings,platform_scheduler,process_program_runner,workflow_due_timer_scheduler,workflow_retry_scheduler]; 6 taken over from the dead JVM
A restarted and rejoined (nodesUp=2 from B); the driver lease stayed with oracle-aa-b, one lock row (no dual owner)
GET /audit/verify-chain intact on A and on B after the crash, survivor writes and rejoin
leader-lease duplicate-key lines over the whole run: A=0, B=0 (followers do not INSERT a held lease)
